meta.scope: Buyer & financing image ads (single-image, plus carousels from Nov 2, 2026) from the Facebook Ad Library (CA), in Ad Library impressions order as first collected. Status badges compare against the Nov 23, 2026 check. Videos and non-applicable angles (sell-my-car, powersports, and $170 bi-weekly / payment-led financing) excluded.
takeaways: New in the Nov 23, 2026 check: 43 new buyer image ads (4 new creatives), plus 56 new ads on excluded sell-my-car and $170-payment angles (not shown). The 4 new creatives are one hook in four UGC executions, launched Nov 17–18: native Reddit posts (r/unpopularopinion, r/carbuyingtipscanada) and Facebook comment threads that tell people to get pre-approved first, before they pick a car ("try doing it in the opposite order", "got my hopes up on a car and the financing fell through"). Headline on all four: "You have more options than you think". The rest of the new buyer ads are new Library IDs of creatives already in the dashboard (repo frost/lot graphics, unsold-inventory clearance, official-notice story cards, rental and credit). No new powersports image ads this week.

New in the Nov 2, 2026 check: 73 new image ads (9 new creatives). The biggest launch (Oct 29–30) is three text-only 9:16 "official notice" story cards with 15 ads: "Insider notice: the order matters", "The expensive year" and "Official retirement announcement" for an aging car. All three push "get pre-approved first", which brings the "Car Shopping Made Easy" angle to images for the first time. Also new: an "Official demo vehicle statement" card, "Used car prices are FINALLY dropping", and 3 carousels (clearance car collages and customer-delivery photos).

Repo cars are the workhorse angle: 48 of 136 ads (15 unique creatives), including 5 of the top 10 and 23 of the top 50 by impressions. Counting rentals, demos and ex-fleet too, the "cheaper source than a regular car" family is 74 ads.

The top-ranked buyer ad by impressions (#2 overall) is a used-rental tweet-style post ("Don't buy a new car, buy a used rental car instead!"), followed closely by repo cars (#4) and unsold-inventory clearance (#6).

Bad or any credit is the near-universal offer: it appears on 30 of 59 unique creatives, plus $0 down (10) and pre-approval in minutes (9). All 136 ads click through to the apply.canadadrives.ca pre-approval form.

"Don't buy X… buy Y instead" is the signature pattern interrupt, used across repo, rental, demo and fleet ads (12 creatives). The same hooks get reshot in many formats: handheld signs, words in snow or frost, tweet posts, cartoons, gradient text.

The creative style is low-fi and native rather than branded: lot-banner photos (13 creatives), words written on cars (10), bold promo graphics (9), handheld signs (7), customer quotes (5), vehicle collages (4) and tweet-style UGC (3).
Seasonal and geo: 12 creatives use winter or snow imagery, including a "buy in fall/winter" pro-tip (3 creatives). Geo-targeting on static images is rare: only one newcomers-to-Canada ad.

texts:
Looking for a great deal on a used vehicle? 

Consider buying a used demo vehicle. A demo vehicle is a car that has been used by the dealership or manufacturer for display purposes, test drives, or as a loaner vehicle for service customers. Here are some reasons why someone might consider purchasing a used demo vehicle:

Lower price: Demo vehicles are typically sold at a discounted price compared to brand new cars. Even though they might have some mileage on them, the savings can be significant, making them more affordable for budget-conscious buyers.

Relatively new and well-maintained: Demo vehicles are usually late-model cars that have been on the road for a relatively short time. They are often well-maintained and kept in excellent condition since the dealership uses them to showcase their products.

Fewer previous owners: Unlike traditional used cars that may have had multiple owners, demo vehicles generally have only been driven by dealership staff or potential customers on test drives.

Manufacturer's warranty: Most demo vehicles are still covered under the original manufacturer's warranty, providing added peace of mind to the buyer.

Upgraded features: Demo vehicles often come with additional features and options that were used to showcase the car's full potential. As a result, buyers may get access to premium features at a lower price compared to custom-ordering a new vehicle.

Immediate availability: Unlike new cars that might require waiting for production and delivery, demo vehicles are readily available at the dealership, allowing buyers to drive away sooner.

Demo vehicles come in a wide range of makes, models, and years. Whether you're in the market for a compact car, a spacious SUV, or a sporty sedan, we can help you find the perfect car and get a great deal.

meta.scope: Video ads from the Facebook Ad Library (CA), sorted by total impressions (135 ads tracked incl. stopped, 61 unique videos across 6 angles; sell-my-car, powersports and $170 bi-weekly payment angles excluded). Status badges compare against the Nov 23, 2026 check. Rank = position in the Ad Library video impressions sort when first collected; it is a separate ranking from the image ads. Transcripts are automatic (Whisper) and may contain small errors.
takeaways: New in the Nov 23, 2026 check: 22 new buyer video ads and 1 new video, plus 11 new ads on excluded sell-my-car angles (not shown). The only new buyer video is another city cut of the 10-second handwritten hatch template: "Don't buy a new car in Regina… buy a used repo instead" (Library start date Oct 31, 2025; first captured this week). The other new buyer ads are new IDs of videos already in the dashboard (demo walk-and-talks and PiP, the clearance voiceover + phone-demo template, long-form creator credit explainers, and the ex-rental handheld sign).

New in the Nov 2, 2026 check: 35 new video ads and 12 new videos, all first seen this week (several have older start dates). The clearance voiceover template was re-voiced for Quesnel, Cranbrook and Revelstoke, plus 2 cuts with no city. The repo "Don't buy a new car in <city>… buy a used repo" clip was reshot for Brandon, Winnipeg and Fort Saint John. Also new: two green-screen creator videos ("If you're shopping for a new car, you need to check out this site"), an 86 s creator repo tip, and a new cut of the "$30k/year" credit comment-reply.

One cheap template owns the top of the video ranking: a 19-second voiceover ("If you're looking for a cheap car in <city>, now is the perfect time to buy… massive year-end inventory clearance deals… before someone else gets the car you want") over the same Bronco, dealer-lot and phone b-roll. It is re-voiced for 11 towns (13 cuts, 16 ads) and holds 7 of the top 10. 7 of the 13 cuts run with repo-car copy, so the video sells timing while the caption sells repos.

Repo cars still take #1: a 10-second clip with no voiceover, "Don't buy a new car in Calgary… buy a used repo instead", handwritten on a car's rear hatch. It was reshot for Grande Prairie, Kamloops and Golden. Repo is 9 videos and 15 ads, 12 of them in the top 50.

Long-form creator videos work: 6 talking-head videos of 80–88 s (14 ads) rank #7, #9, #11, #17, #25 and #48. The same bearded creator in a pink jacket films from his driver's seat, often replying to a TikTok-style comment ("I only make $30k/year… buying a car is impossible", "When is the best time to buy a car in Canada?").

Credit is the biggest video angle by ads (9 videos, 21 ads). It is framed as "get pre-approved first so you're never turned down at the last step" ("Your credit is just a number, not a verdict"). Pre-approval in minutes appears in 38 of 47 videos, and all 81 video ads click through to apply.canadadrives.ca.

Video is where local targeting lives: 22 towns are named in voiceovers, copy or link captions ("Cheap Cars in Kingston"), concentrated in Alberta (11 videos), then Saskatchewan, BC, Ontario and Nova Scotia.
The newest video bet is ex-demo cars: 8 UGC videos and 17 ads, all launched Sep 22 – Oct 16 ("Nobody really talks about this…", "I thought this was a scam at first"), with a best rank of #39.

Production is native and lo-fi: 39 of 47 videos have voiceover with burned-in captions, and the median length is 18.6 s (8 are ≤10 s). 21 are creator-led (talking head, PiP over car b-roll, walk-and-talk) and 2 are motion graphics. There is no polished brand spot.
meta.mix_note: Videos lean harder than images on credit/pre-approval (26% of video ads vs 15% of image ads), clearance/timing (22% vs 10%) and demo cars (21% vs 4%). Images lean on repo cars (35% vs 19%), real-payment proof (20% vs 0%), used rentals (8% vs 4%) and ex-fleet (7% vs 0%). "Car shopping made easy" (testimonials, review cards, a friend's referral) was video-only until Nov 2, 2026, when it arrived on images as text-only "official notice" story cards.

Consider buying a repo car, also known as a repossessed car. Repo cars are vehicles that have been taken back by lenders due to the previous owner's failure to make loan payments. While some may hesitate to purchase a repo car, there are several compelling reasons why it can be a wise decision.
